function: Over-the-air aggregation of local gradients over a MIMO uplink: low-rank gradient factorization (Ota-LC) with analog over-the-air computation, ZF/LMMSE beamforming and error feedback (p. 3-4).
system: Server with 8 antennas, K = 10 devices with 8 antennas each, block-fading MIMO uplink, 20 dB SNR; no RIS; band not stated (p. 4).
method: Federated learning of ResNet18 (supervised classification); low-rank gradient compression via one warm-started Jacobi SCA iteration per round, analog over-the-air computation, error feedback (p. 3; p. 4).
data_channel: Custom i.i.d. CN(0,1) MIMO channels, constant per round, CSI known at server (p. 2; p. 4); CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, i.i.d. and Dirichlet non-i.i.d. splits (p. 4).
test_conditions: Same dataset for training and testing; SNR 20 dB, half of 10 devices per round; sweeps of channel uses and SNR 10-40 dB (p. 4; p. 6).
baselines: SGD without compression; five compressors with error feedback: Ota-CS [10], Ota-RLC [16], PowerSGD [14], Top-K [7], Rand-K [8] (p. 4; p. 5).
metrics: Test accuracy versus total channel uses (r = 20), versus channel uses N_cu, and versus SNR; communication overhead needed for 70% accuracy (p. 5; p. 6).
complexity: Local update O(nmr); uplink overhead O(nr+mr) instead of O(nm); benchmark orders compared: Ota-CS O(mn(m+n)), Ota-RLC O(nmr(m+n)), PowerSGD O(nmr), Top-K O(mn log(mn)) (p. 3; p. 5).
openness: Code released at https://github.com/MingzhaoGuo/Ota-LC (p. 4); channels are simulated.
q1_support: p. 4: "are generated from i.i.d. CN (0, 1) for all k and t": a custom i.i.d. Rayleigh-type MIMO simulator; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 4: "The experiments are performed on the classification task for the Cifar-10 and Cifar-100 datasets": each setting is trained and tested on its own data; p. 5: "for different SNR under T = 250 and Ncu = 4000" is only a sweep.
q3_support: p. 4: "Our method is compared with SGD without compression, as well as with five existing gradient compression methods with error feedback for wireless federated learning"; p. 5 lists Ota-CS [10], Ota-RLC [16] (earlier over-the-air designs), PowerSGD, Top-K, Rand-K; results are test accuracy (Fig. 2, Fig. 3).
q4_support: p. 3: "the local updates (14) require an order O(nmr) of basic operation"; p. 5 compares the orders of the benchmarks (for example Ota-CS O(mn(m+n)), PowerSGD O(nmr)).
q5_support: p. 4: "the code can be found at https://github.com/MingzhaoGuo/Ota-LC"
notes: Area 7: the contribution is the over-the-air aggregation itself (low-rank gradient factorization, analog over-the-air computation, ZF/LMMSE MIMO beamforming, error feedback; p. 3-4), so it passes the federated-learning rules; the learned element is the ResNet18 trained across devices. The extracted text of pages 5 and 6 was unreadable, so both pages were read from the PDF images. q3 rests on the federated rule: Ota-CS [10] and Ota-RLC [16] are earlier published over-the-air aggregation designs, and uncompressed SGD, Top-K [7] and Rand-K [8] serve as non-learned references; the reviewer may judge uncompressed SGD an ideal bound rather than a baseline. Training is repeated per setting (CIFAR-10/100, i.i.d./non-i.i.d.); SNR and N_cu are only swept (p. 5-6).
